full_translation_en:
National Assembly
XXI Session
Complete Details of Proceedings
26 Jestha 2083
Saturday
Meeting Number - 14
The National Assembly's meeting today commenced at 13:20 hrs under the chairmanship of the Honorable Chairperson, Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Members,
(13:20 hrs)
Proceedings commence.
Is it the same in terms of subject matter, or what? First point. But as I said earlier,
Honorable Members,
I was meeting with the available leaders of the parties. Since we said we would come after necessary consultations,
I thought the consultations might have been completed and proceeded, assuming the meeting would take place today. What was the subject? If there was a subject, then the Honorable Members will present their subjects and take their seats, and I will provide time sequentially. I request the Honorable Members to be seated.
Honorable Members, time has been requested to speak during the zero hour. A maximum of three minutes has been allocated for speaking during the zero hour. Now, I will provide time sequentially to the Honorable Members. First, Honorable Member Narayan Dutt Mishra.
Honorable Mr. Narayan Dutt Mishra (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson,
(13:22 hrs)
It is a surprising matter. In Nepal and India, countries with open borders, Nepali citizens farming on land belonging to another country, and land ownership certificates may also be involved. Some of our treaties and agreements may also be having an effect. However, there is no government-level evidence that the sovereign country Nepal has encroached upon the borders of any other country or shifted its border pillars into another country's territory, nor is there any official statement or written proof that India has ever claimed Nepal has encroached upon its territory. When speaking on such matters, what is surprising is that instead of individuals coming forward on the highly sensitive issue of border disputes, the government, and especially the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, must come forward with an official stance. When making such statements, it is necessary to speak based on evidence such as historical documents, maps, and treaties, rather than being swayed by personal emotions. It is surprising that such statements, which weaken national interests, are made, as no country in the world would claim to have encroached upon another country's land.
Honorable Chairperson, the issue of borders is not just a matter for any party, individual, or group; it is a common issue for the entire nation. Therefore, was this statement made against the national interest and on a whim? The issue concerning the country is not a matter for inflammatory speech. The issue of borders is a sensitive matter connected to national sovereignty. When such statements are made in public places like this dignified parliament, it is absolutely necessary for them to be made in a way that strengthens factual evidence and the state's official position. We also want to raise our concerns. The assertion that Nepal has encroached upon borders can weaken Nepal's established diplomatic stance and create confusion. It can affect Nepal's position in future border talks with India, and not only that, it carries the risk of weakening it. Therefore, I humbly request the Honorable Prime Minister to come to parliament (...time expired.)
2
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Renu Chand, time is 3 minutes.
(13:24 hrs)
Honorable Mr. Renu Chand (Communist Party of Nepal): Honorable Chairperson,
(13:24 hrs)
Any country's act of illegally occupying land owned by another country, constructing structures, or expanding borders through the use of force, without mutual consent or legal right, is called encroachment. Have we seen our Prime Minister doing any of these things, and he has said that we have encroached upon the land of our neighbors? He must present proof in the parliament. Do we need to bring proof that we have engaged in such activities on the land of our neighbors? 'Encroachment' and 'cross-hold' are different things. Practical matters between people are different; encroachment done by using the army, by crossing political boundaries, by crossing diplomatic boundaries, is different. As Prime Minister, he should have known this first. He has learned it late. From whom did he get the information that we have encroached on the border? How did this knowledge come about? The Prime Minister must present the source to the parliament. He has made a mistake, thinking he would go viral in a cinematic style; the Prime Minister's speech that day was a complete flop, like a poorly written script.
The Prime Minister's statement is against national integrity, against Nepal's sovereignty, against the constitution, damaging to the self-respect of Nepalis, and detrimental to relations with neighbors. Therefore, the Prime Minister must apologize in the parliament. The House recognizes the PM. I also want to urge the government, through the government, to the party of the Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) not to make the mistake of saying 'I will speak on behalf of the PM' as a second blunder, a second mistake. And let the RSP clarify its party's official stance on nationality. I also urge the Rastriya Swatantra Party to clarify its stance on nationality, regarding the MPs who applauded when the Prime Minister said from the rostrum that we have encroached on the border. To the ministers and colleagues who are saying, 'This is correct, we have encroached on the border,' in a childish manner, I appeal to the Nepali public through the Speaker that the Nepali public should recognize the parliament, recognize such ministers, and recognize such parties. Saying this, I want to raise one more point: a parliamentary inquiry committee should be formed to seriously investigate the Finance Minister regarding the changes in tax rates. "The Finance Minister is not building your dreams" the Nepali people want to say, "He is not building your dreams, the Finance Minister is building his dreams." Therefore, they must be brought under investigation, investigated, and if they have made mistakes, they must be punished. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Meenasingh Rakhala.
(13:28 hrs)
Honorable Mr. Meenasingh Rakhala (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Honorable
(13:28 hrs)
Chairperson, the statement made by the Honorable Prime Minister Mr. Balendra Shah in the parliament on 17 Jestha 2083, "After I became Prime Minister, I realized that not only India has encroached upon Nepal's land, but Nepal has also encroached upon India's land," is not just a casual political remark. It is an extremely serious matter related to nationality, sovereignty, and diplomatic sensitivity. The issue of Nepal's land, borders, and national pride is not a subject for presenting an individual's assumptions, feelings, or personal opinions. It is a matter related to historical facts, evidence, maps, treaties, agreements, and national consensus. Statements coming from the chief executive of the nation on such sensitive issues can have serious repercussions not only within the country but also internationally. Nepal's political parties, parliament, and all Nepali people have remained united in their stance on Nepali territories, including Kalapani, Lipulek, and Limpiyadhura. It is unfortunate and objectionable that such a statement has come from the Prime Minister in a situation where Nepal's official stance is being weakened.
If the said statement is based on facts, the government must present the official evidence related to it to the parliament and the public. If it is an unconstitutional personal opinion, the Prime Minister must immediately withdraw the statement, provide an explanation, and seek an apology from the Nepali people. Making statements that undermine the nation's pride, national interest, and diplomatic dignity is not in line with the responsibilities and accountability of leadership. Therefore, the Prime Minister must take the necessary steps to regain the public's trust by taking moral responsibility for his statement, and if necessary, show the courage to even resign as a moral responsibility.
4
Nationality is a matter above any party, individual, or government. No individual who raises questions about Nepal's land, sovereignty, and national pride can be acceptable to the Nepali people. Therefore, our party's belief and demand is that the statement made by the government must be immediately withdrawn, the parliament addressed, and if possible, he should resign. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Tul Prasad Bishwakarma.
(13:31 hrs)
Honorable Mr. Tul Prasad Bishwakarma (Rashtriya Janamorcha): Honorable
(13:39 hrs)
Chairperson, the Finance Minister has presented the Financial Bill in this esteemed house. And within 24 hours of presenting the Financial Bill, 16 pages of that Financial Bill were mysteriously removed overnight, and a different bill was presented with fewer pages. This is being widely reported in the press. The main reason for removing these 16 pages is the significant manipulation and irregularities in the tax rates. I believe this is perhaps the first incident in Nepal's parliamentary history. The Finance Minister has removed the budget he presented from the website at his own discretion, removed 16 pages, and then prepared and presented it again. This is the first such incident. Therefore, the irresponsible act committed by the Finance Minister is extremely irresponsible. What is his interest in this act? Under whose pressure did he do this? An investigation must be conducted. Similarly, 774 BYD electric vehicles have been imported into Nepal during that time. It is reported that customs officials seized them after they entered. There are reports of billions of rupees being transacted in this matter. Therefore, I want to condemn the irresponsible acts being carried out at one's own discretion, and I want to demand that this incident be seriously investigated. For this, a separate investigation committee should be formed, I want to place my demand through you, Honorable Sir. I want to reiterate my point that it should be investigated seriously, the truth should be ascertained, and those who have made mistakes should be punished. Saying this, I want to conclude my brief remarks. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Members, others will also speak, won't they?
(13:34 hrs)
During the zero hour. How did you know? Please sit down now, Honorable Members. I am announcing. Has the zero hour ended or not? It has not completely ended. Other Honorable Members may have also given their names, please sit down now. First, please announce whether it has ended or not. Whether the zero hour has ended or not, that is your job, why are you in such a hurry?
Honorable Members, the process of speaking during the zero hour concludes here. No, it is not otherwise. There is a procedure, there is a system. It will proceed in a certain way. Parliament is something that proceeds within a system.
Some, perhaps party-based.
Honorable Members, you have been continuously raising your issues and your subject matters here. Now, the process of repeating the same issues is also continuing. Now, how long are we going to hold the National Assembly hostage in this manner? I don't know if I can say so much here, but one thing that the Constitution of Nepal, the general public of Nepal, Nepal's civil society, and the intellectual class all understand is this: if there is only one character, only one, then why would there be two houses? This is what the general public understands.

The public. Somewhere, someone, either the government or the House of Representatives, somewhere there was a mistake or something happened somewhere, the responsibility to correct it lies with the National Assembly. This is a common understanding. It is the understanding of all of us. I think we have been operating in accordance with that understanding, and we have been successful. Again, this does not mean that we have failed; we have been successful. The National Assembly has acted like the saying 'striking the iron while it's hot' when there was a political deadlock. I said that in some cases we have come up with a new approach. Now, in the meantime, as the Chairperson, I have repeatedly spoken with the government's representatives, the Finance Minister, and the Law Minister. How can this be resolved? The government must also take initiative as soon as possible. Discussions have been held repeatedly with the leaders of the political parties, but no conclusion has been reached yet. Therefore, it is not just about any individual, but neither the government nor we in the National Assembly have been successful so far. Therefore, my request is to keep presenting the issues, present them with seriousness, and draw the government's attention. The government's representatives, the honorable ministers, are present in every session. And today, I once again make a special request to the honorable minister to take this matter to the government and present it with seriousness. This cannot be done in a fun way; the country will not run like that. Let us all be responsible in our respective places. Let everyone be responsible in their respective places. This is my special request. Therefore, to move forward with today's proceedings, I request the honorable members to cooperate and to help move forward according to today's agenda by remaining in their seats. To the honorable members, to please remain in their seats. Honorable members, we had just arrived here. With some honorable members of the party, yes, with the available honorable members. It wasn't a party meeting, but after meeting with some honorable members of the party and the available honorable members, it was said that 'we will try as much as possible.' I thought it might happen. Even so, honorable members, if there is a need for consultation among the parties, please ask for time; I am ready to provide ample time. Let's postpone the meeting for half an hour, an hour, and let's all think positively about moving forward with today's meeting, honorable members. If time is needed, let's provide it. Let's postpone it for some time and move forward. If that is also a possibility, honorable members, please stand up and ask for time. I will give you time to speak. If not, if it's easy, please sit down easily and cooperate in moving forward according to today's agenda, honorable members. Honorable members, if I still need some time for discussion, if you want to ask for time, honorable members, please ask for time. I requested that the meeting be postponed for some time, for a few hours, and then moved forward today. However, there was no request for time from the honorable members. In the meantime, I also have some complaints. I mean, not just here, but the way the political situation is developing in the country, the public is not feeling it. There is no consultation from the government's side with the parties, nor do the parties consult with the government. They come to the same house, protest, or present their views. If it is adjourned, the Speaker or the Chairperson adjourns it, and they go home. Tomorrow, whenever they are called, they come. This should not happen. I want to draw the attention of the government side, the honorable ministers, that the government should also take initiative with promptness to solve the problem in a way that the Nepali people can feel it. The parties also, this country belongs to the parties too. The parties should also move forward with a bit more awareness. This is my special request. Instead of blaming others from here, let's all realize that this problem is a common problem for everyone. And now, like this, our sessions, this session, are becoming a hostage, and the Nepali people and the entire country seem to be held hostage when viewed from the outside. Let's end this kind of situation. We are all formed by a common effort. Let's sit down, honorable members. Let's sit down once and move forward with the work. Then, I think an environment for debate will also be created. I think an environment will also be created for discussion between the ruling party and the opposition, or between the government and the houses. Therefore, let's sit down, honorable members. The next meeting of the National Assembly will be held on Thursday, Jestha 28, 2083, at 1:15 PM, and this meeting is adjourned. (Thereafter, the next meeting will be held on Thursday, Jestha 28, 2083, at 1:15 PM, and this meeting is adjourned.) Adjourned: 13:46.

sections.name: Opening
sections.summary_en: The session began at 13:20 hrs under the chairmanship of Narayan Prasad Dahal. The chairperson announced the commencement of proceedings and informed members about the provision for speaking during the zero hour, allocating three minutes per speaker.

speakers.name: Narayan Prasad Dahal
speakers.topic: Opening the session and announcing zero hour procedures

sections.name: Zero Hour
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Narayan Dutt Mishra raised concerns about statements made by the Prime Minister regarding border disputes with India, emphasizing the need for official government stances and evidence-based discussions. Honorable Member Renu Chand criticized the Prime Minister's statements as anti-national and demanded an apology, also calling for an investigation into tax rate changes and the Finance Minister's actions. Honorable Member Meenasingh Rakhala echoed concerns about the Prime Minister's border remarks, calling them detrimental to national sovereignty and demanding accountability, including potential resignation. Honorable Member Tul Prasad Bishwakarma demanded an investigation into the Finance Minister's alleged manipulation of the financial bill and the import of electric vehicles.

speakers.name: Renu Chand
speakers.topic: Prime Minister's statements, tax rate changes, Finance Minister

speakers.name: Meenasingh Rakhala
speakers.topic: Prime Minister's border statements, national sovereignty

speakers.name: Tul Prasad Bishwakarma
speakers.topic: Financial bill manipulation, tax rates, electric vehicles

sections.name: Adjournment
sections.summary_en: The chairperson announced the end of the zero hour and noted that members' issues have been continuously raised. The chairperson questioned the necessity of two houses if there is only one character, implying a lack of differentiation or purpose.

speakers.name: Narayan Prasad Dahal
speakers.topic: Concluding zero hour and reflecting on parliamentary structure

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The Chairperson addressed the National Assembly, emphasizing its role in correcting government and parliamentary mistakes. He highlighted the Assembly's success during political deadlocks and urged for serious discussions and government attention to ongoing issues. The Chairperson also proposed postponing the meeting to allow for party consultations if needed, but noted the lack of requests for time.

speakers.name: Chairperson
speakers.topic: Role of National Assembly, political deadlock, government accountability, need for consultation

sections.name: Adjournment
sections.summary_en: The Chairperson announced that the next meeting of the National Assembly would convene on Thursday, Jestha 28, 2083, at 1:15 PM. The current meeting was then adjourned.

speakers.topic: Announcing next meeting date and adjournment
